question: The 'Special Food Grain Production Programme (SFPP) on Pulses' was implemented during the year ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1988-89**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Special Food Grain Production Programme (SFPP) on Pulses** was launched in **1988-89** by the Government of India to address the issue of inadequate production of pulses in the country.
 
• The programme aimed to increase the production of pulses through **focused interventions**, including better technology adoption, improved seed distribution, and enhanced farming practices.
 
• This initiative was part of a broader effort to ensure **food security** and reduce dependency on imports of pulses, which were a crucial source of protein for the Indian population. *Hence, the correct answer is 1988-89.*
 
• The programme targeted specific regions where pulse cultivation was feasible and promoted **research and development** in pulse farming to improve productivity.
 
• The SFPP on Pulses was integrated with other agricultural development programmes to align efforts and resources effectively. *Hence, this initiative has had a significant impact on pulse production.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Pulses in Agriculture and Nutrition:**

 
 
• **Pulses** are a vital source of **protein** in the Indian diet, especially for vegetarians. They are also rich in essential nutrients like **fiber, vitamins, and minerals.**
 
• India is one of the largest producers and consumers of pulses, but demand often exceeds supply, leading to **imports** to meet domestic needs.
 
• The SFPP on Pulses was introduced to improve **self-sufficiency** in pulse production and reduce reliance on imports.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Pulse Production:**
 
 
• In addition to the SFPP, the government has implemented various schemes such as the **National Food Security Mission (NFSM)** to promote pulse production.
 
• Under the NFSM, subsidies are provided for **quality seeds, fertilizers, and farm machinery** to enhance pulse cultivation.
 
• Research institutions like the **Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR)** contribute to the development of better pulse varieties and farming techniques.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Pulses:**

 
 
• Pulses are **leguminous crops** that improve soil fertility through **nitrogen fixation**. This makes them an essential component of sustainable agriculture.
 
• Common types of pulses grown in India include **chickpeas (gram), pigeon peas (arhar), lentils (masoor), mung beans, and urad.**
 
 
 
• **Impact of SFPP:**
 
 
• The SFPP contributed significantly to improving pulse yields and reducing the **yield gap** in pulse cultivation.
 
• It emphasized the use of **high-yielding varieties** and the adoption of modern farming practices.
 
• The initiative also helped farmers increase their income by providing access to better resources and technologies.
